silky-terrier.citable_stat: A Silky Terrier's first year costs $3,000–$6,000 including puppy price ($1,200–$2,500), with monthly food costs of $30–$55 and annual grooming ranging from $150 (DIY-heavy) to $780 (professional every 6–8 weeks), making grooming the dominant ongoing cost for this breed rather than food.
silky-terrier.name: Silky Terrier

skye-terrier.citable_stat: A Skye Terrier puppy from a reputable breeder costs $1,800–$3,000, with first-year total expenses of $3,500–$6,500 including supplies, vet care, spay/neuter, and grooming; food runs $50–$70 monthly for a 35–45 lb adult, and professional grooming every 8–12 weeks totals $300–$600 annually for the long coat.
skye-terrier.name: Skye Terrier

soft-coated-wheaten-terrier.citable_stat: A Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier costs $5,160–$10,670 in the first year including a $3,000–$6,500 puppy, professional grooming at $400–$700 annually (6–7 sessions at $65–$100 each), mandatory PLN/PLE monitoring at $100–$200, and pet insurance at $400–$900, with ongoing annual costs of $1,600–$3,000.
soft-coated-wheaten-terrier.name: Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier

spanish-water-dog.citable_stat: A Spanish Water Dog costs $3,300–$6,100 in the first year including puppy price, food for a 31–49 lb adult at $400–$700 annually, vet care at $400–$800, and pet insurance at $400–$800, with ongoing annual costs of $1,500–$2,800 thereafter; breed rescue placements run $250–$600 as an alternative to breeder puppies.
spanish-water-dog.name: Spanish Water Dog

spinone-italiano.citable_stat: A Spinone Italiano puppy costs $1,500–$2,500 from a reputable breeder, with first-year total expenses of $3,550–$6,400 including food ($550–$900 annually), routine vet care ($500–$900), and pet insurance ($500–$1,100); the breed's 62–85 lb size pushes most categories toward the upper end of mid-size breed costs.
spinone-italiano.name: Spinone Italiano

staffordshire-bull-terrier.citable_stat: A Staffordshire Bull Terrier from a DNA-tested breeder costs $2,500–$5,000 for the puppy alone, with first-year total costs of $4,090–$7,980 including food at $350–$550 annually and pet insurance at $350–$700 annually; the compact 24–38 lb frame keeps food costs moderate at roughly 1.5–2.5 cups of kibble daily.
staffordshire-bull-terrier.name: Staffordshire Bull Terrier

standard-poodle.citable_stat: A Standard Poodle costs $4,500–$9,500 in the first year including puppy price, with professional grooming running $600–$1,200 annually and food approximately $50–$80 per month; first-year vet care including spay/neuter and breed-specific screening (hips, eyes, thyroid) runs $500–$950.
standard-poodle.name: Standard Poodle

standard-schnauzer.citable_stat: A Standard Schnauzer puppy from a reputable breeder costs $1,500–$3,500, with rescue adoption at $200–$500; first-year costs including food ($500–$800), veterinary care ($400–$800), grooming ($550–$1,000 professional or $120–$250 for DIY clippers), and pet insurance ($400–$900) vary significantly based on geography and grooming method chosen.
standard-schnauzer.name: Standard Schnauzer

swedish-vallhund.citable_stat: A Swedish Vallhund puppy from a reputable breeder costs $1,200–$2,200, with first-year total expenses (including puppy price) ranging from $3,142–$5,872, while rescue adults typically cost $150–$350 and food runs $35–$55/month for a 20–35 lb dog.
swedish-vallhund.name: Swedish Vallhund

tibetan-mastiff.citable_stat: A Tibetan Mastiff puppy costs $1,500–$5,000 from a breeder, with rescue adoption at $300–$800 (typically including spay/neuter and vaccines). First-year food runs $1,200–$1,800 annually, grooming $300–$600 per year, and routine veterinary care $400–$700 annually for an adult weighing 70–150 pounds.
tibetan-mastiff.name: Tibetan Mastiff

tibetan-spaniel.citable_stat: A Tibetan Spaniel costs $2,751–$5,205 in the first year including puppy purchase, with food running $25–$40/month and grooming ranging from $0 (DIY) to $160–$390 annually (professional).
tibetan-spaniel.name: Tibetan Spaniel

tibetan-terrier.citable_stat: A Tibetan Terrier costs $3,310–$5,670 in the first year, with professional grooming every 6–8 weeks at $75–$120 per session forming a lifelong recurring expense, and pet insurance at $400–$700 annually recommended due to hereditary eye conditions like Primary Lens Luxation.
tibetan-terrier.name: Tibetan Terrier

toy-fox-terrier.citable_stat: A Toy Fox Terrier costs $2,500–$4,500 in the first year including acquisition, with food running $25–$45 per month and pet insurance $25–$50 per month if enrolled; rescue adoption runs $150–$350 versus breeder puppies at $1,000–$2,000.
toy-fox-terrier.name: Toy Fox Terrier

vizsla.citable_stat: A Vizsla's first year typically runs $2,800 to $5,500, with food for a 44–65 lb dog costing roughly $40–$60 per month for quality kibble, and professional grooming being genuinely optional due to the breed's short, single-layer coat.
vizsla.name: Vizsla

weimaraner.citable_stat: A Weimaraner costs $3,200–$6,500 in the first year including acquisition, preventive care, and gastropexy (a prophylactic surgery for deep-chested breeds); large-breed food runs $60–$80 monthly, and the short coat requires minimal grooming at under $50 annually.

welsh-springer-spaniel.citable_stat: A Welsh Springer Spaniel costs $2,450–$4,850 in the first year, with food for a 35–55 lb adult running $350–$600 annually and pet insurance at $300–$700 annually, though the breed's elevated risk for glaucoma and hip dysplasia makes early insurance enrollment the highest-leverage financial decision.
welsh-springer-spaniel.name: Welsh Springer Spaniel

welsh-terrier.citable_stat: A Welsh Terrier puppy from a reputable breeder costs $1,200–$2,200, with rescue alternatives at $150–$400; the wiry coat requires professional grooming every 8–12 weeks at $55–$150 per session ($250–$700+ annually), and food costs run $35–$55/month for this 20-pound breed.
welsh-terrier.name: Welsh Terrier

west-highland-white-terrier.citable_stat: A West Highland White Terrier costs $4,450–$8,800 in the first year, with food for a 15–22 lb terrier running $200–$400 annually, but professional grooming every 6–8 weeks and pet insurance ($350–$700 annually) dominate the budget due to the breed's double coat and predisposition to atopic dermatitis.
west-highland-white-terrier.name: West Highland White Terrier

whippet.citable_stat: A Whippet from a reputable breeder runs $2,500–$4,500 for the first twelve months, with food costs roughly $400–$600 a year for a grown dog eating 1.5–2.5 cups of quality kibble daily, and no professional grooming needed due to the smooth single coat.
whippet.name: Whippet

wire-fox-terrier.citable_stat: A Wire Fox Terrier puppy from a reputable breeder costs $1,500–$2,500, with rescue adoption fees running $150–$400; food costs $35–$55 monthly for an 18-pound adult, and professional grooming every 8–10 weeks ranges from $360–$540 annually for clipping to $600–$960+ for hand-stripping.
wire-fox-terrier.name: Wire Fox Terrier

wirehaired-pointing-griffon.citable_stat: A Wirehaired Pointing Griffon costs $2,750–$5,900 in the first year including a $1,000–$2,500 puppy, $450–$750 annually for food, $450–$800 routine vet care, and $400–$900 in pet insurance; ongoing annual costs thereafter run $1,150–$2,200.

wirehaired-pointing-griffon.name: Wirehaired Pointing Griffon

xoloitzcuintli.citable_stat: A Xoloitzcuintli puppy from a reputable breeder costs $2,000–$4,000, with first-year total costs of $3,200–$6,700 for a hairless variety, but ongoing annual costs drop to just $850–$1,900 due to minimal grooming needs and a primitive genetic background free of many hereditary conditions.
xoloitzcuintli.name: Xoloitzcuintli

yorkshire-terrier.citable_stat: Most new Yorkshire Terrier owners land between $2,500 and $5,500 in the first twelve months, with professional grooming every 6–8 weeks running $300–$640 annually and food for a 4–7 lb dog costing $150–$300 in the first year.
yorkshire-terrier.name: Yorkshire Terrier
